findings.finding: Nu is a deposit-funded consumer bank, not a software platform: Q2 2026 IFRS revenue 5,513.2m is mostly interest income on a 39.4bn credit portfolio (cards 26.0, unsecured 10.3, secured 3.1) funded by 45.3bn of retail deposits at 88% of the interbank rate; credit is 41% of gross profit, float 34%, fees 25%. The engine's residual-income lens (book equity, ROE, cost of equity, payout) is the right one; revenue growth is an output of loan growth x risk-adjusted NIM.

Growth is mostly structural share gain and deeper wallet share, not macro: customers +13% y/y to 138.9m, monthly ARPAC +37% to 17.1, portfolio +44% (27.3 to 39.4bn), deposits +24% (36.6 to 45.3bn). Mix component: management states an intentional move into higher-risk, higher-return segments, so part of the NIM gain is bought with credit risk. Macro (Selic 15% peak, now 13.75%) inflates float income and funding cost at once; the residual is not separable from the documents read.

No customer is 10% of revenue; the concentration is geographic: Brazil 91.1% of Q2 2026 IFRS revenue (91.3% of FY2025), Mexico 7.2% (+79% y/y), other 1.7%. Earnings and book are in BRL and reported in USD, so a BRL move translates almost one-for-one into USD profit and book.

Q2 2026 net income 1,061m rests on an IFRS effective tax rate of 14.2% (175.2m on 1,236.3m pre-tax) against 27.6% a year earlier and 25.8% for FY2025 (996.7m on 3,868.4m); H1 2026 is 11.8% (258.1m on 2,190.6m). The reconciliation shows a 42.5% statutory Brazilian rate offset by a 671m Q2 deferred-tax benefit, 114m from lower-taxed entities, 60m interest on capital and 183m 'other amounts' (foreign tax credits, tax-exempt sovereign bond interest, incentives). At the FY2025 rate H1 2026 profit would be about 1,625m instead of 1,933m (about 16% lower): do not annualize Q2; the normalized ROE is roughly 26-28%, not the reported 33%. CSLL rises to 20% from 2028 (Complementary Law 224/2025), a further headwind.

Credit is deteriorating at the margin: NPL 90+ 6.9% (+35 bps q/q, the highest of the last seven quarters), NPL 15-90 4.8%; ECL expense 1,482.2m in Q2 vs 1,012.2m (+46%, faster than the portfolio's +44%); H1 ECL 3,200.2m vs 1,985.7m. Management attributes the q/q move to seasonal migration and an intentional expansion into riskier segments; the allowance is 6.6bn with 244% 90+ coverage. The Brazilian household default rate hit a record 8.09% in September 2026 (6.89% a year earlier), so the system-wide cycle is turning the same way.

Regulatory capital is the binding constraint on growth and buybacks: the Brazilian prudential conglomerate's CET1 fell from 13.0% (Dec 2025) to 11.9% (Jun 2026), Tier 1 14.4% to 13.4%, CAR 16.6% to 15.7%, as RWA grew 14.7% (31.1bn to 35.7bn) against CET1 capital +5.4% (4.05bn to 4.26bn); excess over the minimum 1.85bn. Mexico capital ratio 14.9% and Colombia 15.3% (minimum 10.5%). The 1.0bn buyback (500.4m done, 499.6m left to June 2027) competes with this capital. The residual-income engine does not model RWA or CET1 (stated open item).

Nu gives no numeric revenue, NIM, cost-of-risk or earnings guidance; the only stated target is an efficiency ratio of about 20% for FY2026 (Q2 19.5%, Q1 17.6%, Q2 2025 21.3%) and a risk-adjusted NIM 'in the same region' (12.4% in Q2, 9.5% in Q1). There is no guidance track record to adjust by. US spend is capped at about 100 bps of the efficiency ratio (call summary, secondary).

The quarter review flags negative operating leverage: operating expenses grew about 66% y/y against revenue +50% (IFRS), from return-to-office real estate, marketing and international expansion (Mexico bank launch, US). The profit growth of +67% therefore leans on margin mix and the lower tax rate, not on cost leverage.

Mexico became a full multiple bank on 6 Aug 2026 (15.8m customers, ARPAC about 12.3, deposits 5.7bn down by design, loan-to-deposit 35%); Brazil banking license via the 20 Jul 2026 agreement to buy Banco Porto Real is pending Central Bank approval; the US launch (Sep 2026) has no revenue evidence. These are separately sized options, not base value.

Founder-CEO Velez holds about 74% of the votes through Class B shares; the CFO changed in mid-2026 (Rob Livingston on the Q2 call) and the CTO resigned on 23 Oct 2026 (stays to 12 Nov). Diluted shares were flat y/y (+0.1%): the buyback offsets SBC (H1 SBC 216.8m vs buybacks 500.4m); no dividend.

Piotroski 5 of 7 (mixed); Altman, Beneish and ROIC are not computable from companyfacts and are not meaningful for a bank (deposits are operating funding). ROE is the return metric: FY2024 about 28%, FY2025 about 30% on reported profit; the FY2021-FY2022 loss years belong to the pre-scale phase and pull any 'own median' far below today's level.

economics.reason: Revenue growth comes from customer and wallet-share gains (customers +13%, ARPAC +37%, portfolio +44% y/y) in an under-banked, concentrated market, not from a price or volume cycle; the consumer-credit cycle is real and is carried as a risk to ROE (bear), not as a revenue cycle.
